common_name: Dragon Heart Cranesbill (Magenta-Purple Geranium with Black Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Dragon Heart is a vigorous psilostemon-type hybrid that spreads readily and benefits from room to sprawl.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Dragon Heart bears a profusion of two-inch magenta-purple flowers, each marked with a striking near-black center, from late spring through summer on a fast-growing, sprawling clump. Bred from Geranium psilostemon and G. procurrens parentage, it inherits the vigor and saturated flower color of psilostemon along with a looser, more spreading habit useful for scrambling through shrubs or covering ground quickly. Foliage turns rich crimson in fall. Cutting the plant back hard after the first flush encourages tidier regrowth and often a second round of bloom. It is generally trouble-free, drought-tolerant once established, and rarely bothered by deer or rabbits.

common_name: Nimbus Cranesbill (Lavender-Violet Geranium with White Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Nimbus is a large, vigorous clarkei x collinum hybrid that needs generous spacing to show off its mounding habit.

directions: Plant in moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, though it tolerates full shade as well. Nimbus produces wide-open, lavender-blue to violet flowers with fine dark red veining and a small white center over finely dissected, attractive foliage that emerges yellowish-green in spring before turning mid-green. A hybrid of Geranium clarkei and G. collinum, it forms a large, floriferous, mound-forming clump that blooms heavily from early to late summer and holds RHS Award of Garden Merit recognition for garden performance. Give it room, as it spreads considerably wider than many hardy geraniums. Cut back after the main flush to tidy the plant and encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Azure Rush Cranesbill (Compact Sky-Blue Rozanne-Type Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Azure Rush is a compact, mounding sport of the Rozanne lineage that stays neater than its parent.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Azure Rush bears two-and-a-half-inch, lighter sky-blue flowers with fine red-purple venation over lobed, semi-evergreen foliage from early summer to frost. It arose as a naturally occurring sport from a Geranium wallichianum x himalayense 'Rozanne' hybrid, discovered in Germany, and shares its parent's exceptionally long bloom season and sterility, which keeps the plant flowering continuously without setting seed. Compared to Rozanne, Azure Rush has a more compact, mounding habit with shorter internodes, making it tidier and lower-growing, well suited to container culture and smaller border spaces. It needs little deadheading and tolerates heat well once established.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Spinners forms a wide clump of deeply cut foliage and benefits from generous spacing.

directions: Plant in any moderately fertile, well-drained soil, avoiding waterlogged sites, in full sun or partial shade. Spinners, a 1990 Geranium pratense hybrid selected at England's Axletree Nursery, forms a dazzling two-and-a-half-foot-wide clump of deeply dissected foliage topped from early May through most of the summer with one-inch, cup-shaped flowers of rich violet-blue. Its long bloom period and bold, saturated flower color have made it a long-standing favorite for mixed borders. Remove spent flowering stems and tired foliage through the season to encourage fresh growth and continued bloom, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Sweet Heidy Cranesbill (Trailing Multicolor Wallichianum Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Sweet Heidy has a slightly trailing habit and works well spilling over walls, containers, or border edges.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade. Sweet Heidy bears bowl-shaped flowers with white centers surrounded by pink that fuses into blue, all overlaid with dark veining; blossoms open pink and mature to purple with a white eye, blooming repeatedly from early summer to frost. Bred by Dutch nurseryman Marco van Noort and named for his wife, it descends from the breeding program that produced the popular Geranium 'Jolly Bee,' crossing pink- and blue-flowered forms of G. wallichianum with pink-flowered relatives. The plant has a slight trailing habit, making it useful as a groundcover or for spilling over container edges and underplanting shrubs and roses. Deadhead lightly to encourage continued rebloom.

common_name: Sirak Cranesbill (Lilac-Purple Geranium with White-Blotched Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Sirak forms a vigorous, spreading clump and holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun or a little shade. Sirak, a hybrid of Geranium gracile and G. ibericum raised in the garden of German plantsman Hans Simon, bears abundant five-petaled, lavender-pink to lilac-purple flowers with darker veining and a bright white central blotch, produced heavily from late spring to midsummer over deeply lobed foliage. The vigorous, two-foot-wide clumper is a magnet for bees and holds the Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for its dependable garden performance. Shear back after the main flush to tidy the mound and encourage sporadic rebloom, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
